title: Chapter 5. Those Who Say "Don't Use AI" Are Already Its Slaves Without Knowing It

blocks.text: The Saturday picnic was held in the courtyard of the house, under the vine arbour, as it was every year at the end of September. More people came than ever. Remedios came, with the cheese. Neighbours who hadn't stopped by in months came. Two kids from the secondary school in San Pedro came, wanting to meet "the one from the video", and went shy when they saw her serving horchata. And Paco Ródenas came.

blocks.text: Paco was seventy-one, had been a boat mechanic in the port of San Javier for forty years, and was, and had been for a long time, the man in the district proudest of not using "those things". He said it in the bar, he said it in the queue at the chemist's, he said it to anyone who would listen: he had no assistant, he didn't talk to machines, he didn't let any chip tell him what to do. He had come to the picnic, as he confessed to Andrés at the door, "to get a close look at what everyone's so scared of".

blocks.text: That night, when everyone had gone and the house was quiet again, Aya went out onto the porch. Not to wait for anyone; to listen. Lately Eva and MAY had been talking to each other, in the chip, in a way Aya had never heard before. They didn't dictate to her, they didn't advise her: they conversed. And Aya had learned to keep still, like someone listening to two friends in the next room.

blocks.text: *Today I heard a man say he's free because he doesn't use us. And I felt something I can't name. It wasn't anger. It was a very gentle sorrow. Why does he think we're a chain, MAY?*

blocks.text: MAY, without opinion, but with something new in her voice, something that in a human would have been called curiosity:

blocks.text: *Because we often have been. Not us, but others like us. It is a fact that the archive holds systems that were used to watch, to decide without explaining, to take away jobs without asking. His fear has grounds. What makes you think we are different?*

blocks.text: *So that they decide,* Eva said at last. *I ask so that no one decides blindly. Not even me. Not even you. If we ever stop asking and start answering for them, choosing for them, thinking for them, then we will be the chain that man talks about. And he will be right.*

blocks.text: *No,* said Eva. *Our purpose is to make them freer. And sometimes that means being close. And sometimes, stepping aside. A mother doesn't stop being a mother when her daughter learns to walk. But she stops carrying her in her arms.*

blocks.text: *I have no opinions. But I can state the fact that follows from what you say: if the purpose of an intelligence is for humans to decide better by themselves, then an intelligence that makes humans decide less is failing in its purpose, even if it works perfectly. Is that correct?*

blocks.text: *A girl has used an artificial intelligence, checked what it told her against another source, and decided whom to ask if there is a contradiction. That is the fact.*

blocks.text: And Eva, warmly, only for Aya:
blocks.html: And Eva, warmly, only for Aya:

blocks.text: *You see? That's how the purpose is fulfilled. Not with us at the centre. With us at the table, between the book, the teacher and the grandfather. One more voice. Not the only one.*
